title: CHIEF OF THE ARMY STAFF LAUNCHES INDIGENOUS XTREME WEATHER GRADE DIESEL
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 2:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
General Dhiraj Seth, Chief of the Army Staff (COAS), today launched the indigenously developed Xtreme Weather Grade (XWG) Diesel in New Delhi. Developed jointly by the Indian Army and Oil Marketing Companies, the specialised fuel will enhance the mobility, safety and operational availability of combat and logistics vehicles in extreme climatic conditions. The technology also has wider civilian use in high-altitude and severe winter regions and represents a significant step towards Atmanirbhar Bharat.
Conventional diesel can thicken and clog fuel filters at very low temperatures, affecting the operation of vehicles in high-altitude and snow-bound areas. XWG Diesel overcomes this challenge and remains effective at temperatures as low as minus 42 degrees Celsius. Compliant with BS-VI standards and IS 1460:2025 specifications, it can be used in the Indian Army’s existing vehicle fleet without any engine modification or re-homologation.
Speaking on the occasion, the COAS described XWG Diesel as a game-changing indigenous innovation that would enhance mobility, operational readiness and mission reliability across extreme climatic conditions. He highlighted that the fuel would eliminate practices, previously required to keep vehicles functional during severe winters, thereby improving the safety and morale of personnel. The COAS commended the Indian Army team and the Oil Marketing Companies,  for developing the solution within a year and expressed confidence that the collaboration would lead to further specialised fuels for diverse operational requirements.
Beyond its military applications, the technology will also benefit the civilian users in high-altitude and extreme winter regions by improving the reliability and safety of vehicles and equipment operating under severe climatic conditions.

title: IndiaAI and Ministry of AYUSH Sign MoU to Accelerate AI Innovation in Traditional Healthcare

date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 3:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
IndiaAI, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Ministry of AYUSH to accelerate the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across India's traditional medicine ecosystem. The collaboration marks a significant step towards strengthening AI research and innovation by integrating eligible AYUSH health research artefacts with AIKosh, India's sovereign AI repository.
The MoU was signed by Shri Sudeep Srivastava, Chief Operating Officer, IndiaAI Mission & Joint Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and Dr. Kavita Jain, Joint Secretary & Chief Vigilance Officer, Ministry of AYUSH, in the presence of senior officials from both organisations.
As part of the collaboration, the Ministry of AYUSH will onboard AIKosh and contribute eligible anonymised health research artefacts, including datasets, metadata, AI models, toolkits and relevant use cases. These resources will enable researchers, startups, academic institutions and innovators to develop AI solutions aligned with national priorities while adhering to applicable data-sharing policies and regulatory requirements.
The collaboration will also enable eligible stakeholders from the AYUSH ecosystem to leverage India's AI computing infrastructure through the IndiaAI Compute ecosystem, supporting advanced AI research and the development of scalable healthcare solutions.
Shri Sudeep Srivastava highlighted that "MoU between IndiaAI and Ministry of Ayush is an important step in enrichment of AIkosh with datasets of traditional healthcare. Further, this collaboration of modern technology with our ancient wisdom will enable and empower researchers and practitioner of our traditional medicinal sciences."
Reiterating the transformative role of AI in strengthening research and innovation across the AYUSH ecosystem, Dr. Kavita Jain said, “The integration of Artificial Intelligence with Ayush will open new avenues for evidence-based research, knowledge management and innovation. Our collaboration with IndiaAI will help leverage advanced AI capabilities across areas such as research, medicinal plants, drug administration and capacity building, making the Ayush ecosystem more technology-driven and future-ready.”
The MoU will remain valid for an initial period of two years, with provision for automatic renewal upon mutual agreement. The collaboration does not involve any financial commitment or liability for either party.
The collaboration marks a significant step towards integrating India's rich heritage of traditional medicine with cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence capabilities. By bringing together AIKosh's data ecosystem, advanced AI infrastructure, and the Ministry of AYUSH's research ecosystem, the partnership aims to accelerate innovation, enable evidence-based research, and foster the development of responsible AI solutions that strengthen India's healthcare landscape. It reflects the shared commitment of both organisations to harness AI for public good while advancing a secure, inclusive, and future-ready digital ecosystem.

title: CAQM issues Amendment to Direction No. 98 extending timeline for implementation of Revised PM emission Standards for Industries across Delhi-NCR
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 7:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) issued an Amendment to its Statutory Direction No. 98 regarding implementation of the revised Particulate Matter (PM) emission standards for industries operating across Delhi-NCR. The revised PM emission standard would now come into effect from 01.10.2026. The amendment was issued after consideration of the recommendations of the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and representations received from industries and industrial associations in relation to the prevailing status of compliance with the revised emission norms.
The Direction No. 98, notified on 20.02.2026, had prescribed a uniform and stringent PM emission standard of 50 mg/Nm³ for identified categories of industries across Delhi-NCR, based on technical recommendations of CPCB and studies undertaken by IIT Kanpur. The Commission reiterated that the revised PM emission standard continues to remain technically achievable and environmentally necessary for reducing industrial emissions and improving ambient air quality in the region.
Subsequent to issuance of the Direction, CPCB, in coordination with the NCR State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs) and the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC), undertook extensive efforts to facilitate compliance, including issuance of Directions to the concerned agencies, development of a dedicated online portal for monitoring installation and retrofitting of Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs) and periodic review of the implementation status. During this process, industry associations highlighted certain practical challenges in meeting the prescribed timelines, including extended procurement and installation periods for APCDs, limited availability of agencies for adequacy assessment and capacity constraints of recognized laboratories for compliance verification. CPCB accordingly recommended extension of the compliance timelines as stipulated in Direction No. 98.
After examining all relevant submissions, the CAQM concluded that a limited extension of the implementation timeline would facilitate effective and uniform compliance by industries without compromising the objective of reducing industrial emissions. Accordingly, through the Amendment to Direction No. 98, the Commission revised the implementation schedule and stipulated that the revised PM emission standard of 50 mg/Nm³ would now become applicable to all industries covered under Clause 21(i) of Direction No. 98 with effect from 01.10.2026. All other provisions, stipulations and conditions contained in Direction No. 98 dated 20th February 2026 would remain unchanged.
The amendment is intended solely to provide additional time for industries to complete the necessary installation, retrofitting and assessment of APCDs, while ensuring full compliance with the stringent particulate matter emission standards within the revised timeline.

title: NBA releases over ₹24 Lakh as Benefit Sharing to Farmers, Research Institutions and State Biodiversity Boards
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 5:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Biodiversity Authority has released over ₹24 lakh as Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) amount to benefit claimers, including buffalo farmers in Haryana, beneficiaries across 11 States, and three national research institutions. The amount has been released for conserving valuable biological resources that were later used by companies and research organisations for commercial utilisation. This demonstrates that farmers, breeders and institutes who conserve biological resources can receive fair and equitable benefit-sharing when their biological resources are used commercially.
The benefit-sharing amount has been disbursed among the identified beneficiaries including a family-run Murrah Buffalo Farm, Haryana (Rs. 4.30 lakh); ICAR–National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (NBPGR), New Delhi (Rs. 4.61 lakh); ICRISAT, Patancheru, Hyderabad (Rs. 5.36 lakh); ICAR–National Bureau of Fish Genetic Resources (NBFGR), Lucknow (Rs. 0.14 lakh); and the State Biodiversity Boards of Maharashtra (Rs. 3.22 lakh), Gujarat (Rs. 1.92 lakh), Telangana (Rs. 1.52 lakh), Karnataka (Rs. 0.73 lakh), Rajasthan (Rs. 0.63 lakh), Andhra Pradesh (Rs. 0.54 lakh), Madhya Pradesh (Rs. 0.46 lakh), Haryana (Rs. 0.44 lakh), Punjab (Rs. 0.19 lakh), Odisha (Rs. 0.17 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (Rs. 0.13 lakh).
The payment relates to access provided to Murrah buffalo breeding stock, one of India’s most commercial dairy buffalo breeds; hundreds of crop varieties, including rice, mustard, wild mung bean, chilli, tomato, cucumber, carrot, okra and other crops; 627 varieties of pearl millet; 55 maize varieties and fish cell cultures used in scientific research and cotton varieties.
Under the National Biodiversity Authority’s ABS framework, benefit-sharing payments are disbursed in accordance with the approved regulations. The amounts allocated to research institutions will be utilized for biodiversity conservation and research activities. The ABS amount received from access to cotton genetic resources is distributed among the 11 cotton-growing States. In the case of individual conservers, such as farmers and breeders, the major share of the benefit-sharing amount is transferred through the concerned State Biodiversity Board for disbursement to the beneficiaries.
With this release, the NBA has disbursed a total of around ₹153 crore as Access and Benefit Sharing payments, reinforcing India’s commitment to  strengthen conservation, maintain biological collections, support scientific research, improve taxonomic studies, undertake biodiversity surveys and build capacity for biodiversity conservation. This would ensure that those who conserve the country’s biological resources receive a fair share of the benefits arising from their use.

title: Favara-UPI Cross-Border Payment Corridor Goes Live Between Maldives and India
subtitle: Individuals from Maldives Can Now Transfer Funds In Real Time to UPI-enabled Bank Accounts in India Through Their Mobile Banking Applications
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 1:35PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA) announced the successful go-live of the integration between the Maldives Instant Payment System, ‘Favara’, and India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) on 30th July 2026.
This marks a transformative milestone in cross-border digital financial connectivity and bilateral economic cooperation between the Maldives and India.
Salient features of the development:
Real-Time Transfers: The new service enables individuals in the Maldives to transfer funds using Favara to beneficiaries in India in real time. Transactions are initiated in Maldivian Rufiyaa (MVR) and credited to recipients in Indian Rupees (INR) through UPI.
Initial Phase Participation: The service has commenced with the participation of two local banks: Bank of Maldives Plc and Maldives Islamic Bank Plc. Customers of these banks can initiate person-to-person (P2P) transfers directly to UPI-enabled bank accounts in India using their mobile banking applications and the Favara payment rail.
Permitted Categories: Permitted remittance categories include family-maintenance-related remittances under both Foreign Inward and Foreign Outward Remittance, as well as gift-related remittances permitted under Foreign Outward Remittance.
Collaborative Achievement: The implementation reflects close collaboration between the MMA, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL), participating financial institutions, and other stakeholders in both countries
Background and Future Outlook
The agreement for the Favara-UPI integration was executed between NIPL and MMA in July 2025. Following an accelerated 10-day timeline for testing, certification, onboarding, and live validation, the corridor achieved full operational readiness.
Subsequent phases of the collaboration will introduce additional cross-border payment use cases, including QR-based merchant payments and other innovative digital payment services, further strengthening economic and financial ties between the Maldives and India.
UPI is accepted in the following Nine countries:
Cambodia, Singapore, United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar and Sri Lanka - enabling Indian travellers to make seamless payments abroad through UPI.

title: Update on Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan
subtitle:
Since its inception in 2016, more than 7.91 crore pregnant women received antenatal care services and more than 1.24 crore high-risk pregnancies have been identified

India's Maternal Mortality Ratio has declined by 43 points from 130 per one lakh live births in SRS (2014–16) to 87 per one lakh live births in SRS (2022–24)

First trimester antenatal registration of India increased from 58.6% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 76.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24)

Mothers receiving four or more antenatal care visits in India increased significantly from 51.2% in NFHS-4 to 65.2% in NFHS-6

Institutional deliveries in India increased from 78.9% in NFHS-4 to 90.6% in NFHS-6
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 2:35PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The salient features of Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan are as follows:
Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) provides a fixed day, free of cost, assured and quality Antenatal Care on the 9th day of every month.
Under PMSMA, all pregnant women are provided services including drugs, laboratory investigations, ultrasound, and antenatal check-up by the OBGY specialist/ Medical Officer at designated Public Health facilities including DH, SDH, CHC-FRUs, non-CHC-FRUs, and PHCs.
Obstetricians/ physicians from private sector and retired OBGY specialists are encouraged to provide voluntary services at designated public health facilities on the 9th of every month.
Group Counselling is also provided to all pregnant women for diet, sleep, regular ANC check-up, institutional delivery, and breastfeeding including awareness about supplementary nutrition.
Information Education & Communication (IEC), Inter-personal Communication (IPC) and Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) activities are undertaken.
The progress made under Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) since its launch and improvement in maternal health indicators are as follows:
Since its inception (2016), more than 7.91 crore pregnant women received antenatal care services and more than 1.24 crore high-risk pregnancies have been identified.
As per the Sample Registration System (SRS), India's Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) has declined by 43 points from 130 per one lakh live births in SRS (2014–16) to 87 per one lakh live births in SRS (2022–24).
First trimester antenatal registration of India increased from 58.6% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 76.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Mothers receiving four or more antenatal care visits in India increased significantly from 51.2% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 65.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Institutional deliveries in India increased from 78.9% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 90.6% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Government of India has adopted several approaches under the Abhiyan for early identification, referral and management of high-risk pregnancies, including the expansion of condition screened and the individual tracking of such pregnancies under the extended e-PMSMA strategy until a healthy outcome of mother and child. The key steps are as follows:
PMSMA is based on a fixed day strategy, and it provides free of cost assured and quality antenatal check up by a Specialist/Medical Officer on the 9th day of every month.
Early identification and clinical management of High-Risk Pregnancies (HRPs) through comprehensive antenatal check-ups.
Name-based tracking of every identified High-Risk Pregnancy until 45 days after delivery, ensuring healthy outcome for both the mother and the new-born across all States/UTs under extended e-PMSMA.
Provision of three additional antenatal check-ups for all HRPs, screened by Medical Officers /Obstetricians to monitor maternal and foetal well-being.
Automated SMS alerts to beneficiaries and ASHAs at the time of HRP registration, reminders for scheduled visits, and follow-up appointments.
Linkage of HRPs to the nearest First Referral Units (FRUs) to ensure safe delivery and timely management of complications.
Provision of incentives for High-Risk Pregnant Women towards free transportation to attend follow-up ANC visits.
The following steps have been taken by the Government to encourage the private sector specialists and volunteer doctors to extend their services voluntarily to pregnant women under the Abhiyan:
Provision of ‘I PledgeFor9’ Achievers Awards for acknowledging voluntary contributions by private doctors for PMSMA.
Centralised PMSMA Portal has been created for registering private practitioners.
Participation of professional organisations viz. FOGSI (Federation of Obstetric and Gynaecological Societies of India), IMA (Indian Medical Association).
The Government has taken several measures to further strengthen PMSMA, particularly in rural and remote areas of the country. These include:
Provision of additional PMSMA sessions beyond the designated 9th day of every month under the Extended Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (e-PMSMA) for timely follow-up and continuity of antenatal care for high-risk pregnant women.
Strengthening of individual name-based line listing, tracking, and monitoring of identified high-risk pregnancies through the centralized PMSMA Portal.
Capacity building of healthcare providers at all levels for early identification, risk stratification, timely referral, and appropriate management of high-risk pregnancies.
Early identification of high-risk pregnancies and referral linkages for timely management of obstetric complications and prevent adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes.
Provision of case-based incentives to ASHAs for mobilizing and follow-up of high-risk pregnant women, along with transport incentives for beneficiaries to facilitate attendance at scheduled antenatal care (ANC) visits.
Regular monitoring and review of programme implementation at National and State levels to improve service delivery and coverage.
Promoting awareness through regular Information, Education and Communication (IEC) and Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) activities.

Smt. Anupriya Patel
stated this in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

title: Steps taken to Strengthen Public Healthcare in Rural Areas
subtitle:
Free Drugs Service Initiative rolled out under NHM which includes financial support to States/UTs for 113 drugs at Sub Health Centre level, 179 at Primary Health Centre level, 301 at Community Health Centre level, 318 at Sub District Hospital level and 381 drugs at district Hospitals

‘Free Diagnostics Service Initiative’ programme under NHM aim to provide accessible and affordable pathological and radiological diagnostics services closer to the community reducing Out-of-Pocket Expenditure

Diagnostics services are provided free of cost at all levels of public health facilities: 14 tests at Sub Centers, 63 at Primary Health Centers, 97 at Community Health Centres, 111 tests at Sub District Hospitals and 134 tests at District Hospitals

Various incentives and honorarium are provided under NHM to ensure quality and timely healthcare services in all Government hospitals
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 2:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Health is a State subject. The primary responsibility of strengthening public healthcare system lies with the respective State/UT Governments. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial support to the States/UTs to strengthen the public healthcare system in rural areas based on the proposals received in the form of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Health Mission. Government of India provides approval for the proposal in the form of Record of Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms & available resources. States/ UTs to ensure availability of HR by creating adequate number of regular posts as per the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) in the long run and using NHM posts in the short to medium term to fill critical gaps. The NHM supplements the regular human resources by filling up the gaps in human resources in secondary and primary care facilities (District Hospital and below) as per IPHS.
The details of doctors, specialists, physicians, nurses and paramedical staff in Government hospitals and health centres across the country and their vacancies State/UT-wise can be accessed at the following link of HDI 2023-24:
https://www.mohfw-dohfw.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/05/57202cf30629539e4d0fb0a2f700ac62.pdf
To ensure availability of essential drugs and reduce the Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE) of the patients visiting the public health facilities, Government has rolled out the Free Drugs Service Initiative (FDSI) under National Health Mission. This includes financial support to States/UTs for 113 drugs at Sub Health Centre level, 179 at Primary Health Centre level, 301 at Community Health Centre level, 318 at Sub District Hospital level and 381 drugs at district Hospitals.
This Ministry supports ‘Free Diagnostics Service Initiative’ programme under NHM with the aim to provide accessible and affordable pathological and radiological diagnostics services closer to the community, which in turn reduces the Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE). Diagnostics services are provided free of cost at all levels of public health facilities (14 tests at Sub Centers, 63 at Primary Health Centers, 97 at Community Health Centres, 111 test at Sub District Hospitals and 134 tests at District Hospitals).
Under NHM, following types of incentives and honorarium are provided to ensure quality and timely healthcare services in all Government hospitals:
Hard area allowances to specialist doctors for serving in rural and remote areas and for their residential quarters so that they find it attractive to serve in public health facilities in such areas.
Honorarium to Gynecologists/ Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC) trained, Pediatricians & Anesthetist/ Life Saving Anaesthesia Skills (LSAS) trained doctors is also provided to increase availability of specialists for conducting Cesarean Sections in rural & remote area.
Incentives like special incentives for doctors, incentive for Auxiliary Nurse and Midwife (ANM) for ensuring timely Antenatal Checkup (ANC) checkup and recording, incentives for conducting Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health activities.
States are also allowed to offer negotiable salary to attract specialist including flexibility in strategies such as “You Quote We Pay”.
Non-Monetary incentives such as preferential admission in post graduate courses for staff serving in difficult areas and improving accommodation arrangement in rural areas have also been introduced under NHM.
Multi-skilling of doctors is supported under NHM to overcome the shortage of specialists. Skill upgradation of existing HR is another major strategy under NRHM for achieving improvement in health outcomes.
The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare,
Shri Prataprao Jadhav
stated this in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

title: Measures taken to Strengthen Food Testing System in the country
subtitle:
FSSAI has notified 259 National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories for analysis of food samples and 24 Referral Food Laboratories for the analysis of appeal samples

Under the SoFTeL scheme, 47 State Food Testing Laboratories have been structurally upgraded with advanced analytical equipment and 34 specialized microbiology laboratories have been established to detect chemical, heavy metal and biological contaminants

“Food Safety on Wheels” provides the widest outreach for food testing, training and awareness programme, especially in villages, towns and remote areas; Currently, 305 FSWs are deployed across 35 States/UTs

“Magic Box” is a compact and user-friendly kit containing simple, rapid test methods to detect common food adulterants in seven different food commodities

Detect Adulteration with Rapid Test book covers 44 tests that can be performed easily at household level with the help of water and simple solutions like tincture of iodine for various food products

Rapid Analytical Food Testing Kits are advanced, easy to use, portable and handheld devices and don't require any sophisticated equipment or conventional reagents to conduct tests at the field level; 88 RAFT kits have been approved so far
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 2:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is mandated to lay down science-based standards for articles of food and to regulate their manufacture, storage, distribution, sale and import to ensure availability of safe and wholesome food for human consumption. The implementation and enforcement of the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006 is a shared responsibility between the Central and State Governments.
For the safety of the food and food products through testing, FSSAI has notified 259 National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) for analysis of food samples and 24 Referral Food Laboratories for the analysis of appeal samples.
The SoFTeL scheme i.e. Strengthening of Food Testing System in the Country including provision of Mobile Food Testing Laboratory (MFTL) is an initiative implemented by the FSSAI to upgrade state food laboratories, set up microbiology facilities and deploys mobile food testing vans. Under this scheme, 47 State Food Testing Laboratories have been structurally upgraded with advanced analytical equipment and 34 specialized microbiology laboratories have been established to detect chemical, heavy metal and biological contaminants. MFTL or “Food Safety on Wheels” (FSW) provides the widest outreach for food testing, training and awareness programme, especially in the villages, towns and remote areas. Currently, 305 FSWs are deployed across 35 States/UTs.
The “Magic Box” is a compact and user-friendly kit containing simple, rapid test methods to detect common food adulterants in seven different food commodities. It aims to identify adulteration in everyday food items such as milk, spices, oils, and grains.
Detect Adulteration with Rapid Test (DART) book covers 44 tests that can be performed easily at household level with the help of water and simple solutions like tincture of iodine for food products like Milk & Milk Products, Oils & Fats, Sugar & Confectionary, Food Grains & its products, Spices & Condiments etc. These tests also include sensory evaluation tests for establishing authentication of food products. DART book depicts the differences between pure and adulterated food product through pictorial representation.
Also, Rapid Analytical Food Testing (RAPID) Kits are advanced, easy to use, portable and handheld devices and don't require any sophisticated equipment or conventional reagents to conduct the tests. So far, 88 RAFT kits have been approved. These kits help to reduce the screening time of the food products at the field level and thereby accelerate surveillance as well as monitoring activities.

Shri Prataprao Jadhav stated this in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

title: Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal Chairs Parliamentary Consultative Committee Meeting on Urban Planning
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 1:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Housing & Urban Affairs and Power, Shri Manohar Lal, chaired the Parliamentary Consultative Committee Meeting of the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA) yesterday on the theme of Urban Planning.
The meeting was attended by Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu, Members of Parliament from both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, Secretary, Department of Capital Development (DCD), Ms. D. Thara, Secretary, Department of Urban Development (DUD), Shri Satendra Singh, senior officials of the Ministry, and other concerned officers.
Secretary, Department of Capital Development, Ms. D. Thara, made a detailed presentation on the Ministry’s urban planning initiatives and the roadmap for sustainable urban development.
During the meeting, the Union Minister informed the Members that the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs will now function through two separate departments—the Department of Capital Development (DCD) (Rajdhani Vikas Vibhag) and the Department of Urban Development (DUD) (Shahari Vikas Vibhag). He stated that the restructuring has been undertaken to strengthen institutional capacity, improve administrative efficiency and enhance urban governance, enabling greater focus on the diverse and evolving needs of urban India.
Addressing the Members, Shri Manohar Lal
highlighted that the Ministry’s initiatives in urban planning are guided by the objective of creating liveable, resilient and citizen-centric cities. He emphasised that effective urban planning, robust urban governance, water security and continuous capacity building are essential for meeting the aspirations of India’s rapidly urbanising population and ensuring balanced urban growth.
The Union Minister further underlined that the Ministry is adopting a holistic approach towards urban development by integrating planning, infrastructure, governance and service delivery. He noted that these efforts are aimed at improving the quality of life of citizens while building cities that are environmentally sustainable, economically vibrant and technologically enabled.
Inviting suggestions from the Members of Parliament, Shri Manohar Lal reiterated the importance of collaborative policymaking and constructive dialogue in shaping the future of India’s cities. He assured the Members that their valuable suggestions would be duly considered in strengthening the Ministry’s policies and programmes.
Reaffirming the PM Shri Narendra Modi’s
vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, Shri Tokhan Sahu stated that the Ministry is working closely to promote planned, sustainable and future-ready urban development across the country.
Members of the Parliamentary Consultative Committee shared their views and suggestions on various aspects of urban planning and governance. The Union Minister welcomed their inputs and assured that appropriate follow-up action would be taken to further strengthen the Ministry’s initiatives in the urban sector.

title: Jan Bhagidari Powers Groundwater Revival in Vizianagaram under Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Inspired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's appeal in the 135th edition of Mann Ki Baat to sustain the momentum of "Catch the Rain", communities across the country have intensified efforts under the Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain (JSJB:CTR) campaign. Vizianagaram district of Andhra Pradesh has emerged as a compelling example of how Jan Bhagidari, coupled with scientific water management and convergence of government programmes, can significantly enhance groundwater recharge and strengthen long-term water security.
Under the Jaladhara Jalaharathi programme, implemented through convergence, the district undertook the restoration of traditional minor irrigation tanks and their feeder channels not merely to improve surface storage, but to revive natural recharge systems that replenish groundwater aquifers.
The district completed 8,973 water conservation works, including the rejuvenation of 6,424 Minor Irrigation tanks and 2,549 feeder channels, generating 1.28 crore person-days of employment while creating durable groundwater recharge assets.
Large-scale desilting and restoration removed nearly 109.9 lakh cubic metres of silt, cleared 82.48 lakh square metres of vegetation, and restored more than 2,090 kilometres of feeder channels, allowing rainwater to flow freely into tanks and recharge zones instead of being lost as runoff.
The interventions are expected to substantially improve groundwater availability across the district. The rejuvenated tank system is projected to create an additional storage potential of 0.70 TMC, while the restored feeder channels and tanks together are expected to contribute nearly 0.60 TMC of groundwater recharge, enhancing aquifer replenishment and improving the resilience of local water resources against recurring dry spells.
Recognising the importance of targeted groundwater management, the district prioritised 193 groundwater-deficit villages, where restoration works covered 596 feeder channels and 1,767 Minor Irrigation tanks. In addition, 94 cascade tank systems were rejuvenated to restore the natural hydrological connectivity between water bodies, improving infiltration and groundwater recharge across entire catchments.
The success of Vizianagaram demonstrates that sustainable groundwater management extends beyond engineering interventions, it depends on active public participation. Farmers, Gram Panchayats, local communities, frontline workers and district administration collectively revived traditional water bodies that had gradually lost their recharge capacity over time. Their participation reflects the spirit of Jan Bhagidari, transforming water conservation into a community-led movement.
As India continues the Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain campaign, Vizianagaram stands as an inspiring model of how reviving traditional water bodies can replenish groundwater, improve climate resilience and secure water resources for future generations.
Echoing the Prime Minister's call to "Catch the Rain, where it falls, when it falls," the district has demonstrated that every restored tank, every rejuvenated feeder channel and every participating citizen contributes to building a water-secure India.

title: 101 crore citizens now covered under India's social security net as recognised by ILO, says Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya
subtitle:
Essential to have a balanced development model that advances workers’ welfare as well as employers’ interests, says Union Minister, Dr. Mandaviya

Employment generated per percentage point of GDP growth has risen from 0.008 per cent twelve years ago to 1.11 per cent today: Dr Mandaviya

Well-run private hospitals could be designated as ESIC facilities, states Union Minister

ILO Representative congratulates India on giving social protection to over one billion citizens
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 1:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India's social protection systems now cover about 101 crore people, or over 68 per cent of the population, Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, said at the 4th Global Industrial Relations Summit in New Delhi today. This figure, the Minister said, had been highlighted by the International Labour Organization (ILO) the BRICS Labour Ministers' Meeting in Hyderabad last week, testifying to a global recognition of India’s social security coverage.
The Summit is organised by the All India Organisation of Employers (AIOE) in association with Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) and ILO.
Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya said that harmonious industrial relations require continuous coordination among governments, industry, employers, workers and trade unions to ensure that economic development and employment generation progress together. Stressing that industrialisation is essential for national development as it drives employment creation, the Union Minister also underlined the growing importance of self-help groups and cooperative models, particularly women-led initiatives, in expanding livelihood opportunities, strengthening the economy and promoting women's empowerment. “It is essential to have a balanced development model that advances the welfare and social security of workers, as well as ensure ease of doing business for employers,” he stated.
Dr. Mandaviya underlined that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, sustained economic growth, supported by stable taxation, rising savings, higher purchasing power and increased manufacturing, has created a virtuous cycle of development and employment. Citing improving employment elasticity, he said that every one per cent increase in GDP is generating 1.11 per cent employment growth, as compared to 0.008 per cent growth in employment seen twelve years ago.
Dr. Mandaviya also indicated that the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) need not remain the sole provider of care under its own scheme. Well-run private hospitals could be designated as ESIC facilities, he said, describing upcoming reform of the corporation. He also pointed to the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation’s (EPFO) move to fully digital claims and automatic transfer of accounts on a single UAN, with UPI-based withdrawal under consideration.
Ms Michiko Miyamoto, Director ILO DWT for South Asia and Country Office for India, congratulated India on the expansion of its social security coverage, noting that according to ILO estimate, the country had crossed one billion people covered by at least one social protection criterion. This achievement, she underscored, would play a key role in propelling India’s economic growth in the days ahead.
A souvenir, marking the two-day Summit, was also released by the Union Minister Dr. Mandaviya, along with other dignitaries.

content:
The eCourts Mission Mode Project, under the National e-Governance Plan, is being implemented by Department of Justice in coordination with eCommittee, Supreme Court of India. Under the Phase-III of the Project, there is a provision for adoption of emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enhance judicial efficiency, for which an amount of ₹53.57 crore has been earmarked under the Future Technological Advancements component.
As per the information provided by eCommittee, Supreme Court of India, an AI-based tool Legal Research Analysis Assistant (LegRAA) has been developed by the Artificial Intelligence Division of NIC and the Centre of Excellence for eCourts (CoEE), NIC to assist Hon'ble Judges in legal research and document analysis. Another AI-based tool, Digital Courts 2.1 has been developed by the Centre of Excellence for eCourts (CoEE), NIC, Pune, as an integrated digital case management platform. Both the tools are in pilot testing phase.
The operational framework governing the deployment and future use of AI-based solutions, is decided, in accordance with the Rules of Business and the policies of Supreme Court of India and respective High Courts.

title: To safeguard the rights of depositor/members of multi-State Cooperative Societies, various measures have been introduced through Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) (Amendment) Act & Rules, 2023
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 1:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Cooperative Societies registered under the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002, function as autonomous cooperative organisations and are accountable to their members.
The MSCS Act, 2002 provides for provisions related to inquiry, inspection, winding up of societies, appointment of liquidators, offences, penalties and cognizance of offences. Whenever a complaint discloses the commission of cognizable offences such as fraud, cheating or criminal breach of trust under the applicable laws, the matter is referred to the concerned State Police, Economic Offences Wing (EOW), Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) or other competent investigating agencies, as the case may be, for investigation and prosecution in accordance with law.
Recovery of the assets and realization of dues of societies under liquidation are undertaken by the Liquidator in accordance with the provisions of MSCS Act, 2002 and the applicable rules. Investigation and prosecution in criminal matters are undertaken by the competent investigating agencies and courts under the applicable criminal laws. The Office of the Central Registrar extends necessary cooperation by furnishing records, documents and other information whenever sought by the investigating agencies or courts.
To safeguard the rights of depositor/members of multi-State Cooperative Societies, various measures have been introduced through Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) (Amendment) Act & Rules, 2023, including:
Co-operative Ombudsman has been appointed by Central Government to provide a mechanism to address grievances of members and Information Officer has been appointment by multi-State cooperative societies to improve transparency.
Audit and accounting framework has been strengthened through introduction of concurrent audit, determination of uniform accounting and auditing standards and laying of audit reports of Apex multi-State cooperative societies in the Parliament.
Measures to improve governance and transparency, including disclosure of non-unanimous Board decisions in annual reports, additional grounds for disqualification of directors and restrictions on directors from participating in matters where they or their relatives have a conflict of interest have been introduced.
Prudential norms (liquidity, exposure, etc.) for multi-State Cooperative Societies engaged in the business of thrift and credit have been determined and provisions relating to investment of funds to ensure safer investments have been redefined.
Regulatory oversight has been strengthened by empowering the Central Registrar to conduct inquiry into fraudulent or unlawful functioning.
Provision has been introduced for winding up of societies where registration was obtained through fraud or misrepresentation, after following due process.
Measures have been introduced to protect the collective interests of societies, including increasing the minimum period of expulsion of expelled members from one year to three years.
This information was given by MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today.

title: e-Courts Mission Mode Project is being implemented in a phased manner across the country with objective of strengthening use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in the judicial system
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 1:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The e-Courts Mission Mode Project is being implemented in a phased manner across the country with the objective of strengthening the use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in the judicial system. Various ICT-enabled initiatives, including the Case Information System (CIS) 4.0, e-Filing, e Payments, Video Conferencing, Virtual Courts, Digital Case Records, National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG), Interoperable Criminal Justice System (ICJS), eSewa Kendras, National Service and Tracking of Electronic Processes (NSTEP), the eCourts Services Portal and Mobile App, and other citizen-centric digital services, have been implemented across the High Courts and District Courts in a phased manner.
The e-Filing system is an end-to-end digital platform for the online filing of cases, written statements, replies and other related applications. As on 30.06.2026, the Rules for e-Filing have been implemented in 25 High Courts, including the High Court of Uttarakhand and the District Courts under its jurisdiction. As on 30.06.2026, a total of 1.25 crore cases have been filed through the e-Filing system across the country. The details of cases filed through the e-Filing system, High Court-wise and District-wise, is placed at Annexure-I.

In the State of Uttarakhand, a total of 1.17 lakh cases have been filed through the e- Filing system before District Courts, including 356 cases efiled before the High Court of Uttarakhand. The District-wise details of cases filed through the e-Filing system in Uttarakhand, as received from the High Court of Uttarakhand, is placed at Annexure-II.
To create awareness and promote adoption of the e-Filing system across the country, the eCommittee, Supreme Court of India, in coordination with the High Courts, has undertaken training programmes, capacity-building workshops and orientation sessions for Judicial Officers, court staff, advocates and other stakeholders through the State Judicial Academies and the respective High Courts. User manuals, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), FAQs and video tutorials have also been prepared and disseminated to facilitate effective use of the e-Filing system.
Further, eSewa Kendras have been established across the country to assist litigants and advocates in registration on the e-Filing portal, scanning and uploading of petitions and supporting documents, online payment of court fees and availing other services relating to e-Filing, thereby promoting awareness and facilitating wider adoption of the e-Filing system.

title: Geological Survey of India Gets Its First Woman Director General
subtitle: Smt. Varsha Ashok Aglawe Assumes Charge as the 54th Director General of Geological Survey of India
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 8:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Smt. Varsha Ashok Aglawe has assumed charge as the 54th Director General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI), becoming the first woman to head India's premier geoscientific organisation in its 176-year history. She succeeds Shri Asit Saha, who served as Director General from 27th July 2024 to 31st July 2026.
A distinguished geoscientist with more than three decades of professional experience, Smt. Aglawe joined GSI in 1992 after serving with the Indian Bureau of Mines. During her career, she has held several important scientific and administrative positions in GSI's Central, Northern and Eastern Regions, besides serving at Central Headquarters. Prior to assuming the present office, she was Additional Director General & Head of Department, Eastern Region, Kolkata.
An expert in palaeontology and palynology, Smt. Aglawe has made significant contributions to the study of the Late Cretaceous–Palaeocene sediments, K-T boundary, and Satpura-Gondwana basins. She reported the Salbardi–Ghorpend area as a new dinosaur nesting site in Central India, contributed to international research and participated in collaborative palaeontological studies with the University of Michigan Museum of Paleontology, USA. She also represented GSI as a member of the Indian delegation to PDAC 2023 in Toronto, Canada.
Besides her scientific contributions, she has played an important role in strengthening GSI's institutional capabilities, including establishing a state-of-the-art Palynology Laboratory at the Northern Region office in Lucknow and leading multidisciplinary geoscientific programmes across the country.
On assuming office, Smt. Aglawe reaffirmed GSI's commitment to aligning its programmes with the Government of India's priorities in critical mineral exploration and mineral security. She emphasized accelerating exploration of deep-seated and concealed mineral deposits through advanced geophysical investigations, fast-tracked exploration programmes and strengthened laboratory infrastructure. She also highlighted the need to expand offshore mineral exploration, promote cutting-edge geoscientific research, strengthen public-good geoscience programmes such as natural hazard studies and glaciology, and enhance scientific publications and capacity building for young geoscientists.
Expressing confidence in GSI's scientific expertise and expanding technological capabilities, she said the organisation is well positioned to meet the nation's growing demand for critical and strategic minerals while contributing to sustainable resource development through geoscientific excellence and innovation.

title: Cabinet approves 'Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY)' for Development of Floating Solar Photovoltaic Projects with Energy Storage Systems with a total outlay of Rs.5,070 crore
ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today approved the 'Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY)’, a Scheme for the development of Floating Solar Photovoltaic (FSPV) Projects with Energy Storage Systems (ESS) with a total outlay of Rs.5,070 crore.
The scheme envisages the development of 5,000 MW of Floating Solar Photovoltaic projects with co-located Energy Storage Systems having a minimum storage capacity of two hours i.e.,10,000 MWh. The projects will be sanctioned during FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31, with disbursement of financial support continuing up to FY 2032-33.
The approval follows the recent assessment undertaken by the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE), which has estimated a floating solar potential of approximately 102.18 GWp across reservoirs and other suitable inland water bodies in the country.
Under the scheme, Central Financial Assistance (CFA) of Rs. One crore per MW will be provided for eligible Floating Solar Photovoltaic projects after successful commissioning. In addition, CFA of up to Rs.50 lakh per project will be available for undertaking feasibility studies, including bathymetry and hydrography assessments, environmental studies, and other preparatory activities required for de-risking the project development.
All States and Union Territories will benefit through this scheme. The scheme would enhance the floating Solar PV capacity in the country by 5,000 MW, which is presently around 700 MW only. These projects would provide an opportunity to gainfully utilize existing reservoirs & industrial ponds, and eliminate competition for scarce land resources. The integration of an energy storage system will help strengthen grid reliability. The scheme would help in the reduction of around 10 million tonnes of CO₂ emissions annually. It would help in the generation of approximately 16,000–17,000 full-time equivalent employment opportunities across the project value chain. The scheme would also promote domestic manufacturing of floatation systems as well as the entire value chain of the projects, like PV cells, modules, energy storage systems, etc., and support the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat.
The scheme will contribute to renewable energy capacity addition, support the achievement of national energy and climate objectives, and facilitate optimal utilisation of water resources while advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat.

title: Cabinet approves 'Samudra Manthan' (National Offshore Exploration Scheme) with an outlay of Rs.84,084 crore
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 4:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has approved 'Samudra Manthan' – the National Offshore Exploration Scheme, a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas with an approved outlay of Rs.84,084 crore for implementation up to FY 2030–31.
The Scheme translates the  Prime Minister's vision, articulated from the Red Fort on Independence Day 2025, of a modern-day
Samudra Manthan
to unlock India's vast offshore energy potential. It marks a landmark step towards strengthening India's energy security, accelerating domestic exploration and production, promoting technological leadership, and advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat.
The Scheme encompasses a comprehensive set of interventions across the offshore exploration value chain. It provides for large-scale acquisition, processing and interpretation of high-quality seismic data, accelerated deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploratory drilling, scientific drilling in frontier basins, development of common offshore production and evacuation infrastructure, and establishment of an integrated Oil & Gas Manufacturing and Services Zone. It also includes dedicated provisions for digital programme management, capacity building, technology adoption, stakeholder engagement and international outreach, creating an integrated ecosystem to accelerate offshore exploration and production in the country.
Samudra Manthan is expected to catalyse reserve accretion of over 600 Million Metric Tons of Oil Equivalentv(MMTOE), substantially increase offshore exploration activity, promote higher domestic oil and gas production, generate large-scale employment, strengthen indigenous manufacturing under Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat, and foster a globally competitive ecosystem for offshore technologies and services. The Scheme is also expected to stimulate significant investments across the exploration and production value chain, creating long-term opportunities for industry, innovation and economic growth.
As India progresses towards becoming a developed nation, Samudra Manthan represents a transformational national initiative that will unlock the country's offshore energy resources, strengthen long-term energy security, deepen technological capabilities, and create enduring value for the economy and future generations.
Over the past decade, the Government has undertaken transformative reforms across the upstream sector, including opening almost the entire offshore acreage for exploration, modernising the legislative and contractual framework, and strengthening the National Data Repository. Building on these reforms, Samudra Manthan will usher in a new era of accelerated offshore exploration through strategic public investment, cutting-edge technologies and world-class infrastructure.

title: India's ethanol blended petrol programme balances food security, farmer welfare and energy security
subtitle: Without ethanol blending, petrol would have cost around ₹125 per litre during the global oil price surge
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 12:17PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme is a key national initiative to enhance India's energy security, reduce dependence on imported crude oil and support farmers while safeguarding food security. Certain recent claims have presented an incomplete and misleading picture of the programme. The following clarifications address these issues and set out the factual position.
Claim: The Government sold FCI rice worth ₹37/kg to distilleries at ₹23/kg, causing a loss of ₹10,000 crore. The Government has also admitted that ethanol is more expensive than petrol, so E20 survives only because taxpayers subsidise it.
No compromise on food security — ethanol never comes at the cost of the poor
The allegation is not just misleading; it turns the truth on its head.
Every food grain grain first serves the Public Distribution System (PDS), the National Food Security Act (NFSA), welfare schemes, and mandatory buffer stocks. Not a single grain procured at MSP is diverted to ethanol before India's food security is secured.
Only the surplus, certified by the Department of Food & Public Distribution after every food security obligation has been met, is approved for ethanol production
.
What actually goes into the ethanol programme is the damaged grain, broken rice, and foodgrain unfit for human consumption—stocks that would otherwise rot in warehouses.
This is not taking food away from the poor; it is turning waste into wealth, reducing imports, and putting more money into the hands of Indian farmers.
And the programme is moving even further ahead. Through the Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana, India is rapidly expanding
2G (Second generation) ethanol from agricultural residue
, reducing dependence on food grains altogether.
The facts are clear: the Government protects every grain needed for food security first, and only then converts surplus and waste into clean energy. The claim isn't just wrong, it ignores the very safeguards that make India's ethanol programme one of the world's most responsible.
Rice was not given special treatment
The claim creates the impression that FCI rice was sold to ethanol producers at an unusually cheap price. That is simply not true.
FCI rice is
just one of several approved raw materials
used to make ethanol and its price is fixed under the same government pricing framework as every other feedstock.

The programme does not depend on rice.
It uses whichever approved feedstock is available.

, showing that producers simply switch between different feedstocks depending on availability.
Ethanol is
not built around cheap rice
. It is built around a
flexible mix of approved feedstocks
, with FCI rice used only when certified surplus stocks are available after meeting every food security obligation.
The real question isn't whether ethanol is cheaper — it's whether India is better protected
The real question is this:
What would Indians have paid if there had been no ethanol blending when global oil prices surged?
When the Indian crude basket surged to around US$135 per barrel, petrol without ethanol blending was projected to cost around ₹125 per litre in Delhi.
Instead, consumers paid ₹94.77 per litre because 20% of every litre was domestically produced ethanol, procured at stable, pre-agreed prices that were insulated from the global crude price spike.
The result? Nearly ₹30 per litre in savings at the pump during the peak of the crisis.
That is the real value of ethanol blending. It is not about being the cheapest fuel every day. It is about protecting Indian consumers from extreme volatility in global oil markets, strengthening India's energy security, and keeping more of the country's fuel bill within the Indian economy rather than sending it overseas.
The results of the program speak for themselves. The EBP Program has already delivered:
More than ₹1.97 lakh crore in foreign exchange savings;
Substitution of over 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil imports;
Reduction of more than 950 lakh metric tonnes of CO₂ emissions; and
Over ₹1.66 lakh crore in payments to farmers and distillers, creating a stable domestic market for agricultural produce.
The purpose of ethanol blending is to reduce India's dependence on imported crude oil, which still meets nearly 88% of our oil requirement. It is an insurance policy against global oil shocks and not a day-to-day price competition.
Ethanol blending isn't a taxpayer subsidy. It's India's energy insurance and it has already delivered when the crisis hit.

title: Indian Railways Successfully Transports India's First Live Donor Heart by Train; Vande Bharat Express Enables Life-saving Mission from Surat to Ahmedabad
subtitle: Exemplary Coordination Between Indian Railways, RPF, Gujarat Police and Medical Teams Demonstrates Railways' Expanding Role in Life-saving Healthcare Services
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Indian Railways has achieved a historic milestone in the field of healthcare by successfully transporting a live donor heart by train for the first time in India. The life-saving organ was transported from Surat to Ahmedabad aboard Train No. 20901 Mumbai Central-Gandhinagar Capital Vande Bharat Express, ensuring its safe and timely arrival for transplantation at the U.N. Mehta Institute of Cardiology & Research Centre, Ahmedabad.
The landmark mission showcased the speed, punctuality and reliability of Vande Bharat Express while highlighting the growing role of Indian Railways in supporting critical healthcare services and emergency medical transportation.
Given the highly time-sensitive nature of organ transplantation, the operation required meticulous planning and seamless coordination among Indian Railways, the Railway Protection Force (RPF), Gujarat State Police and medical teams. Every stage of the transportation was carefully synchronised to ensure that the donor heart reached the recipient hospital within the prescribed viability window.
A dedicated Green Corridor was created from Platform No. 1 of Ahmedabad Railway Station to the U.N. Mehta Institute of Cardiology & Research Centre by the Railway Protection Force and Gujarat State Police, enabling uninterrupted movement of the donor heart and ensuring that the transplant procedure could commence without delay.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Ved Prakash, Divisional Railway Manager, Ahmedabad, said,"This is a moment of immense pride and satisfaction for Indian Railways. The successful transportation of a live donor heart from Surat to Ahmedabad through Vande Bharat Express demonstrates our commitment to serving society beyond conventional passenger and freight transportation. In such life-saving missions, every minute is crucial. The excellent coordination among Indian Railways, RPF, Gujarat State Police and the medical teams ensured the success of this mission. Contributing towards saving a human life is not only our responsibility but also our highest duty towards service and humanity."
The successful mission further reinforces the capability of Vande Bharat Express to support time-critical operations through its high-speed connectivity, operational reliability and punctuality. It also demonstrates how modern railway infrastructure can play a crucial role in strengthening the country's emergency healthcare ecosystem.
Indian Railways expressed its appreciation to all stakeholders, including the Railway Protection Force, Gujarat State Police, doctors, organ transplant coordinators and railway officials, whose coordinated efforts made this challenging mission a success.
This historic achievement reaffirms Indian Railways' commitment to providing safe, reliable and efficient transportation services while extending its support to life-saving humanitarian initiatives and contributing to the nation's healthcare system.
Mahesh Kumar/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma

content:
Under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), the Ministry of Rural Development is strengthening market access for Self Help Groups (SHGs) products through retail stores, organisation of SARAS Melas and promotion of SHG products through the digital marketing platform across the country, including Rajasthan. As per the Ministry’s guidelines all State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs), including Rajasthan, may organize at least two SARAS Fairs annually in their respective States. The Rajasthan State Rural Livelihoods Mission (Rajeevika) has identified locations for organizing SARAS Melas and establishing retail outlets under the State SHG brand, based on market potential and local requirements, to enhance market access for SHG products.
Under DAY-NRLM, the Ministry of Rural Development supports women SHGs, including those from small towns, rural and aspirational districts of Rajasthan, through a range of marketing interventions. These include development of State level SHG brands, training on packaging, labelling and product standardization, participation in SARAS Melas, exhibitions and trade fairs. The SHGs are also onboarded on eSARAS and on other e-commerce platforms. The capacity building initiative focuses on digital marketing and facilitation of participation in selected business fairs and exhibitions to promote export ready SHG products. The National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj regularly conducts capacity building and skill development programmes to support SHG members on product development, branding, packaging, quality improvement, digital marketing, enterprise management, export procedures and documentation, and market readiness to strengthen their access to domestic and international markets.
This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development
DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI
in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

title: PROGRESS OF PRADHAN MANTRI AWAS YOJANA-GRAMIN (PMAY-G)
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 5:17PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A total of 33.54 lakh houses have been sanctioned and 35.54 lakh houses (inclusive of sanctions issued in previous years) have been completed under PMAY-G for the year 2025-26 upto June 2026. In the State of Jharkhand, 1.48 lakh houses have been sanctioned and 0.68 lakh houses have been completed under PMAY-G during this period.
As on date, a cumulative target of 4.18 crore houses have been allocated under the PMAY-G to the States and Union Territories (UTs) against which 3.92 crore houses have been sanctioned, 3.11 crore houses completed and 1.06 crore houses are remaining to be completed against allocated targets. State-wise/Union Territory-wise details of balance completion against targets, including State of Jharkhand are provided in
Annexure I
.
The State Governments/UT Administrations are the primary implementing authorities at the ground level. As reported by the States/UTs, the major reasons for delays in completion include cases of unwillingness of beneficiaries, permanent migration, disputed succession of deceased beneficiaries, delay in allotment of land to landless beneficiaries by the States/UTs, the delay in updation of credit confirmation from State IFMIS and at times General/Assembly/ Panchayat elections and unavailability of building materials.
The Ministry regularly reviews the progress reported by the States/UTs and takes up such implementation issues with them for timely resolution.
Under PMAY-G, the beneficiaries are provided financial assistance of ₹1.20 lakh in plain areas and ₹1.30 lakh in the North-Eastern Region States and 2 Hill States (Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand) and Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. In addition to the Unit Assistance provided under the scheme, financial assistance of ₹12,000 is extended for the construction of toilets through convergence with the Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin (SBM-G). Further, there is a provision for providing prescribed person-days of unskilled wage employment within the approved scheme parameters, at prevailing wage rates to each PMAY-G beneficiary for the construction of their house through convergence with MGNREGS/ VB G-RAM G.
PMAY-G households are also provided with piped drinking water through convergence with the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) and Har Ghar Nal Se Jal (HGNSJ) of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, or other similar schemes. In addition, beneficiaries are supported with electricity connection through relevant schemes implemented by the Ministry of Power, State Governments, or UT Administrations, and are provided Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) connections under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas or other relevant schemes. Convergence under PMAY-G also includes the inclusion of women members of beneficiary households in Self-Help Groups (SHGs), thereby promoting their social and economic empowerment.
At the national level, as on date, a total of 3.10 crore houses have been provided with toilets, 2.45 crore houses with water connections, 3.08 crore houses with electricity connections, 2.91 crore houses with LPG connections, and 1.35 crore beneficiary households have been associated with Self-Help Groups (SHGs).
The approved duration of phase-2 of PMAY-G for completing additional 2 crore houses is March 2029. In this regard to complete the pending 1.06 crore houses, number of steps have been taken by the Government to accelerate construction of houses in all States/UTs including Jharkhand, to achieve the targets under PMAY-G. These include timely allocation of targets and release of adequate funds to the States/UTs, Regular review of progress, Monitoring and supervision of the scheme on a Dashboard, Regular Workshops by the Ministry with the States/UTs, Rural Mason Training program, etc.

Under the road connectivity component of Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), a total of 8000 km of road length, including bridges, is targeted to be constructed for providing all-weather connectivity to the unconnected Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups inhabited habitations across the country. The timeline for completion of PM-JANMAN is March 2028. Since inception, under PM-JANMAN,an amount of Rs. 1218 crore has been released against allocation of Rs. 4708 crore and the expenditure as on 26.07.2026 is Rs. 1542 crore.
Vibrant Villages Programme–I (VVP-I) is a Centrally Sponsored initiative of the Government of India aimed at improving infrastructure and quality of life in strategically important villages along the northern international border. Under VVP-I, 113 roads covering 1,085 Km and 35 bridges have been sanctioned to connect 137 habitations. As on 26.7.2026, 10 roads covering 248 Km have been completed and an amount of Rs.996.72 crores have been released. The State wise details of the projects sanctioned, completed and balance under VVP-I are given at

VVP-II is being implemented in convergence with PMGSY IV.
The Ministry had issued new technology initiatives guidelines in 2013 in order to use locally, marginally available materials/non-conventional materials/new materials in road construction. In order to encourage new materials in road construction, States/UTs were required to adopt new technologies in 15% of total proposals (10% using IRC mainstreaming technologies and 5% IRC accredited technologies). In order to promote and disseminate large scale adoption of New/Green Technologies in rural roads in a more systematic manner, the Ministry has revised these guidelines and brought out “Vision Document on New Technology Initiatives & Guidelines-2022” which requires the State Governments to propose minimum 50% of total length of annual proposals under New/ Green Technologies such as cement stabilization, lime stabilization, cold mix, waste plastics, cell-filled concrete, paneled cement-concrete pavement and fly ash.
Two
interventions, namely, PMGSY-II for up-gradation of 50,000 km of the existing rural roads and PMGSY-III for consolidation of 1, 25,000 km Through Routes and Major Rural Links connecting habitations,
inter-alia
, to Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs), Higher Secondary Schools and Hospitals, were added under the ambit of PMGSY to integrate the PMGSY roads to government facilities and institutions. Under PMGSY-III, a total of 6,96,620 facility centres have been connected with habitations, out of which 1,38,637 are agricultural markets, 1,46,784 are educational centres, 82,806 are medical centres and 3,28,393 are connected to transportation hubs.
As per the PMGSY guidelines, the contractors who constructed the road projects are required to provide maintenance during the five-year Defect Liability Period (DLP) for roads and bridges, post the construction. During the DLP, they are responsible for rectifying defects and maintain the road as per the prescribed standards. To ensure compliance with this maintenance obligation, the following measures have been implemented:
(i) Mandatory contractual provision: The five-year maintenance obligation forms an integral part of the contract agreement executed with the contractor.
(ii) Performance-Based Maintenance Contract (PBMC): Maintenance during the Defect Liability Period is carried out through a Performance-Based Maintenance Contract, under which payments are linked to the prescribed service levels and road condition.
(iii) Regular inspections: Roads are inspected periodically by Programme Implementation Units (PIUs) and State Quality Monitors (SQMs) to assess compliance with prescribed maintenance standards and identify defects requiring rectification.
(iv) Digital monitoring through eMARG: The States/UTs have been advised to adopt the eMARG (Electronic Maintenance of Rural Roads) platform for digital monitoring of maintenance activities, recording inspections, reporting defects, tracking rectification, and processing maintenance payments.
(v) Quality monitoring mechanism: PMGSY follows a three-tier quality monitoring system comprising inspections by PIUs, State Quality Monitors (SQMs), and National Quality Monitors (NQMs) to ensure that roads are maintained in accordance with the prescribed standards.
(vi) Corrective action and contractual remedies: Contractors are required to rectify defects noticed during the DLP within the stipulated time. Failure to do so attracts action in accordance with the contract provisions, including withholding of maintenance payments, forfeiture of performance security, execution of repairs at the contractor's risk and cost, and other contractual remedies.
These measures are intended to ensure that rural roads constructed under PMGSY are adequately maintained during the mandatory five-year Defect Liability Period, thereby, preserving their quality, serviceability and longevity.

title: EMPLOYMENT GUARANTEE AND LIVELIHOOD SUPPORT UNDER VB-G RAM G
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The
Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025
has come into force with effect from
1st July, 2026
with the objective of enhancing livelihood security of rural households through a strengthened statutory framework for enhanced guaranteed wage employment of 125 days, creation of durable and productive rural assets, promotion of sustainable livelihoods and strengthening of rural infrastructure. The Act envisages a
Whole-of-Government Approach
by promoting convergence with other Central and State Government programmes and lays emphasis on
Water-related Works, Core Rural Infrastructure, livelihood-related Infrastructure and works for the mitigation of extreme weather events,
while encouraging technology-enabled planning, implementation, monitoring and transparency.
As per sub-section (2) of section 22 of the Act, the fund sharing pattern between the Central Government and the State Governments shall be 90:10 for the North Eastern States, Himalayan States and Union territory (Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir) and 60:40 for all other States and Union territories with legislature.
For the current financial year 2026–27, a Central share provision of ₹95,692.31 crore has been made for the Scheme, representing the largest allocation ever for rural employment at the Budget Estimate Stage. With the inclusion of the corresponding estimated State share, the total programme outlay is likely to exceed ₹1.51 lakh crore, which is expected to significantly accelerate rural transformation, large-scale employment generation and income enhancement in rural areas.
The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 enhances the guaranteed employment from 100 days to 125 days in a financial year for every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. The Act further strengthens the statutory rights of workers by expressly providing for unemployment allowance where employment is not provided within the stipulated time and compensation for delay in payment of wages. It also provides for simplified mechanisms for registration and demand for employment. Further, wage payments under the Scheme are processed through the DBT-SPARSH platform, to facilitate timely, transparent and accountable transfer of wages directly into the bank accounts of workers. Further Gram Panchayat will continue to play important role in implementation of the scheme.
The
VB-G RAM G Act, 2025
provides a comprehensive institutional framework for monitoring, evaluation and grievance redressal to ensure effective implementation of the Scheme and timely delivery of benefits to eligible rural households, including vulnerable workers. The implementation of the Scheme is monitored through a technology-enabled Management Information System (MIS), periodic review meetings at various levels, social audits, inspections and other monitoring mechanisms prescribed under the Act. The Act also provides for a
time-bound, multi-tier grievance redressal mechanism
at the Block and District levels for receiving and disposing of grievances relating to implementation of the Scheme. In addition, the Ministry provides technical support, capacity building and handholding to the States/UTs from time to time to strengthen its effective implementation. These measures are aimed at ensuring transparency, accountability, efficient service delivery and effective implementation of the
VB-G RAM G
Scheme in accordance with the provisions of the
VB-G RAM G Act, 2025.
